text: Common causes of lameness and movement difficulty: Staphylococcus foot abscess — a swollen abscess on the underside of the foot causes lameness; the microbe lives in soil and survives in stagnant rain puddles; treat by mixing Erythromycin into feed for 5 days. Worms — if an adult duck suddenly goes lame, check whether it has been wormed recently. Injuries/cuts — examine the legs and feet closely (especially the underside); moderate injuries just need cleaning and disinfecting, while serious ones may need feed-mixed antibiotics (Erythromycin, Doxycycline, or Amoxicillin); isolate a lame bird in a small pen with easy access to feed/water to limit its movement while it heals. Vitamin D deficiency — needed for calcium/phosphorus absorption and normal skeleton formation; deficiency causes soft bones and lameness in chicks, who rest in a squatting position and show reluctance to walk with a stiff gait. Swollen joints: Salmonella (Pullorum) causes early-life death in very young chicks, but in older birds can appear as a sub-acute disease with lameness and joint swelling; Mycoplasma's joint form causes lameness, lethargy, reluctance to move, swollen joints, a stilted gait, weight loss, and breast blisters — treat with Tylosin or Doxycycline.
